description: Most road-facing block edges should read as a continuous street wall rather than isolated buildings.
Preserve parks courtyards car parks and service courts as deliberate negative space rather than filling every gap.
Consolidate a minority of adjacent lots into larger apartment church or civic footprints without scaling windows walls or roof components.
Major intersections should usually have an anchored corner building using chamfered L or perimeter massing.
Prefer short attached or nearly attached frontage runs rather than one freestanding building per parcel.
Small gaps should read as alleys or service access; avoid arbitrary medium-sized voids between buildings.
Dense blocks should regularly use U-shape courtyard perimeter or L-shape massing to create authored interior space.
Building height bands should cluster along a block instead of changing randomly at every lot.
Most ordinary buildings should use stepped chamfered L U courtyard or perimeter footprints; plain rectangles are the minority.
No single footprint shape should dominate the district.
Road-facing building edges should approximately follow the nearest road instead of ignoring street geometry.
Keep buildings close enough to sidewalks to form streets while retaining a readable pedestrian edge.
Walls windows stairs rooftop units and facade modules remain approximately constant physical size across all footprints.
Churches civic buildings and distinctive towers should punctuate the city without becoming common.
Recognizable landmarks should usually have breathing room and not appear as randomly repeated special sprites.
Each district should reuse a small coherent set of roof facade and trim families rather than assigning every building an unrelated palette.
Some adjacent buildings should visibly belong to the same construction era while avoiding copy-paste repetition.
Large roofs need fixed-size HVAC skylight bulkhead tank vent and stair modules so they do not read as enlarged flat sprites.
Large merged footprints should contain multiple module types and a clear primary roof feature.
Exact roof facade and clutter signatures should almost never repeat across many buildings.
Water texture and palette must remain visually continuous across generated and protected-map boundaries.
The extension should retain many angled or gently bending streets instead of collapsing into a perfect orthogonal grid.
Zebra bars remain parallel to lane direction and compact relative to road width.
Sidewalk ribbons remain continuous except at legitimate junction and crossing space.
Existing meaningful water and green areas should survive generation rather than being replaced by buildings or roads.
